o.text: From earlier *čimgän (“meadow”), from Proto-Turkic *čïm (“turf”). Compare Turkish çimen, Turkmen çemen, Uzbek chaman, Uyghur چىمەن (chimen).
From Armenian չաման (čʻaman). Compare Turkish çemen.
Ultimately a derivation from Proto-Turkic *yāl-. Cognate with Turkish yalvarmak.
Ultimately from French étymologie, reinterpreted as an adjective.
Borrowed from Classical Persian اهل درد (ahl-i dard).
From əla (“excellent”) + -çı. Probably a calque of Russian отли́чник (otlíčnik); attested since at least 1938.
From Arabic عَلَف (ʕalaf). Doublet of yulaf.

From tərbiyə + -çi.
Calque of Russian воспита́тель (vospitátelʹ).
Present participle compound of qrant (“grant”) + yemək (“to eat”). Calque of Russian грантое́д (grantojéd).
Borrowed from Arabic وَلَد الزِّنَى (walad az-zinā).
